events.did: asked Sydney to fix the problem she had created so that she would show she was willing to commit to the work
events.quote_anchor: You created a problem. I’m asking you to fix it. Not only because it needs doing, but because it will show that you’re willing to commit to the work.

events.did: refused to agree to Gray's treatment, saying she could not
events.quote_anchor: “I can’t,” said Syd, fists balled on her knees.

events.did: swiped the pencil off the desk after an alarm cut Gray off, and drove its sharpened point into his thigh when he blocked the door
events.quote_anchor: Dr. Gray rose, too, and moved to block her way, and she drove the pencil’s sharpened point down into his thigh.

events.did: ran into Noah in the hall, hugged him, and broke the clasp on the gun holstered at his back
events.quote_anchor: her hand found what it was looking for. The sleek black weapon holstered at his back. As her thumb broke the clasp

events.did: pulled the gun free and shot Noah in the chest after telling him she was not a kid
events.quote_anchor: Syd pulled away, sliding the gun free as she looked up at him. “I said, I’m not a kid.”

events.did: fled down the white halls with no signs and no windows, and the world tipped as she turned at a T
events.quote_anchor: there was no way to know how to get there because the halls and walls all looked the same. No signs. No windows.

events.did: found herself in the galley kitchen watching a popcorn packet revolve in the microwave, and realized she was still in the white halls
events.quote_anchor: She straightened, fingers gripping the counter, as if to ground herself. She hadn’t been here, had she? No, she was in the white halls, trying to—

events.did: walked into the living room and sank into a chair with a whisky
events.quote_anchor: instead of passing by, he sank into a chair, a whisky hanging from his fingertips.

relations.did: Gray was treating her as the age she looked and not the age she was, assuming she wanted a father figure when she already had two
relations.quote_anchor: He was treating her as if she was the age she looked, and not the age she was. Assuming she wanted a father figure, when she already had two.

relations.did: Mitch had taught her to fight dirty, using her teeth or anything she could find, because fighting clean is for the ring
relations.quote_anchor: Mitch had taught her, if she was ever in a fight, she should fight dirty.

relations.did: Noah was the smiling stranger from the porch, and his mottled swirl of colors marked him as an EO
relations.quote_anchor: He wasn’t wearing sunglasses anymore, and his eyes gave him away, a mottled swirl of colors that marked him as an EO.

relations.did: she knew he should not be there, that the moment belonged to the months after he had left, and that it was not real
relations.quote_anchor: She knew he shouldn’t be there, knew this, this moment, which was made up of a memory, belonged to the months after he’d left.

numbers.did: how long she has been running: nearly half her life
numbers.quote_anchor: you have been running for nearly half your life. You must be tired.

numbers.did: the number of father figures she already had: two
numbers.quote_anchor: Assuming she wanted a father figure, when she already had two.

numbers.did: the number of rounds she emptied into Noah's chest: seven
numbers.quote_anchor: Seven rounds, and at least one must have gotten through because Noah looked down, brows knitting in confusion as blood soaked through his front.

numbers.who: the agents Sydney met in the hall
numbers.did: the number of agents coming toward her: a pair
numbers.quote_anchor: She hit a T and turned right, only to find a pair of agents coming toward her.

numbers.did: how much room it really was: half a cushion
numbers.quote_anchor: What Mitch declared a Sydney-shaped-space, which really just meant half a cushion in the corner.
